newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: U.S., Australia settle trade row over leather.
newsitem.headline: U.S., Australia settle trade row over leather.

text.p: The United States and Australia said on Sunday they had settled a trade dispute involving leather products.

The agreement, which followed U.S. President Bill Clinton's five-day working holiday in Australia last week, was announced in a joint statement issued by acting U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky and Australian Deputy Prime Minister Timothy Fischer.

"We have reached a satisfactory settlement of the dispute over automotive leather. The agreement is based on an exchange of letters by which Australia has agreed to excise automotive leather from eligibility under the import credit scheme (ICS) and the export facilitation scheme (EFS) by April 1, 1997," the statement said.

Barshefsky and Fischer said that they were "fully satisfied" that the matter was now resolved and said it underscored the strong bilateral relationship promoted by Clinton and Australian Prime Minister John Howard last week.
